# 1. Getting started

<!-- Generated by tools/generate-docs.lisp from docs/manual/chapters.lisp,
     docs/manual/introduction.md and the examples: do not edit by hand. -->

A cog-lisp program is a file of forms, run from top to bottom by the cog-lisp
launcher: `./cog-lisp.sh hello.lisp` on Linux, `cog-lisp.bat hello.lisp` on
Windows. With no file, the launcher starts the REPL.

## The smallest cog-lisp program

`examples/hello.lisp`:

```scheme
(display "Hello from cog-lisp!")
(newline)
```

Its output:

```text
Hello from cog-lisp!
```

## Recursion, and integers that grow past 64 bits

`examples/factorial.lisp`:

```scheme
(define (factorial n)
  (if (= n 0)
      1
      (* n (factorial (- n 1)))))

(define (show-row n)
  (display n)
  (display "! = ")
  (display (factorial n))
  (newline))

(define (count-up from to)
  (if (<= from to)
      (begin
        (show-row from)
        (count-up (+ from 1) to))))

(count-up 0 10)
(show-row 25)   ; a bignum, courtesy of the host's integers
```

Its output:

```text
0! = 1
1! = 1
2! = 2
3! = 6
4! = 24
5! = 120
6! = 720
7! = 5040
8! = 40320
9! = 362880
10! = 3628800
25! = 15511210043330985984000000
```
